_comment: 🧩️ This plugin's contribution to the repository test platform. The framework discovers this file by convention (`testContributionDirName` in 🔣️taxonomy.json) and never names this plugin or any standard it owns. Nothing format-specific lives here: the fifteen norm artifacts are all semio-native, so every (non-)oracle registration and every mutation catalog sits with its own subset, at `🗿️artifacts/<artifact>/🏅️standards/🔖️1/🪆️subsets/✳️any/🔣️oracle.json`. What this root manifest carries is the ONE thing a subset cannot declare for itself: an `oracleHostPackage` reaches a case through its owner's ANCESTORS, and a case owned by `🗿️artifacts/<artifact>` is not a descendant of the subset that declares the catalog.

oracleHostPackages.rationale: 📕️ The ONE independent Python implementation of the norm mutation vocabulary, put on the generated Python host's import path so all fifteen subset adapters IMPORT it instead of each holding a byte-identical copy. It is in-repo source (`path`), never a distribution, so nothing is provisioned and the dependency ratchet classifies it as neither production nor third-party. The fifteen subsets differ in exactly four things — kind list, specification vectors, example document, envelope token — and those four stay with the subset; the derivation rules the engine implements are one committed document for all fifteen, so implementing them fifteen times would have been fifteen copies of a single reading, not fifteen readings. Declared here rather than per subset for the same reason the Rust entry above is: an `oracleHostPackage` reaches a case through its owner's ANCESTORS, and a case owned by `🗿️artifacts/<artifact>` is not a descendant of the subset that declares the catalog.
